Report Description///THIS IS A UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1328447/// THE UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: RELEASED MATERIALS: HEPTANE IS 1950 GALLONS REMEDIAL ACTION: CONTRACTOR HAS BEEN HIRED, RELEASE IS SECURE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION OF INCIENT:CALLER REPORTS A CHEMICAL MIXER MALFUNCTIONED, DISCHARGING 625 GALLONS OF HEPTANE (MAIN COMPONENT OF A PRODUCT CALLED "KINJALE") INTO A CONCRETE CONTAINMENT. THIS MALFUNCTION ALSO CAUSED AN UNKNOWN QUANTITY OF A CEMENT PRODUCT (A HEPTANE, TOLUENE, BARSOL D-100, METHYL ETHYL KETONE MIXTURE) TO BE DISCHARGED. THE TOTAL QUANTITY OF CEMENT RELEASED IS BELIEVED TO BE LESS THAN THE PURE "KINJALE" (HEPTANE) PRODUCT. AN UNKNOWN QUANTITY OF THE "KINJALE" HAS REACHED AN OUTFALL TO SALT CREEK, BUT HOW EXACTLY THIS IS OCCURRING IS UNKNOWN. THIS CONTAINMENT AREA WAS NOT BELIEVED TO HAVE A DRAIN. THE ENTIRE VISIBLE PORTION OF THE CREEK HAS A RED SHEEN/DISCOLORATION (40 FT X 15 FT). THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT/HAZMAT CREW/HEALTH DEPARTMENT ARE ON-SCENE RESPONDING. IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE RELEASE IS SECURED. 200 EMPLOYEES HAVE BEEN EVACUATED, AND THE STREET GOING TO THE FACILITY IS CLOSED.

THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS BELIEVED TO HAVE BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH SHIP POLLUTION AND WAS OBSERVED APPROXIMATELY 2.30 NM SOUTHWEST FROM ISLE AUX HERBES, ALABAMA. IT APPEARED AT THE NORTHEASTERN END OF A VESSEL’S TRACK, IDENTIFIED BY THE VISIBLE SHIP WAKE EXTENDING TO THE SOUTHWEST. IT STOOD OUT AGAINST THE OCEAN BACKGROUND WITH A SHIMMERY, SEGMENTED APPEARANCE AND WIDENED WITH DISTANCE FROM THE POTENTIAL VESSEL. ITS TOTAL LENGTH MEASURED 1.84 NM, INCLUDING ALL SEGMENTS, AND 0.08 NM AT ITS WIDEST POINT. AT THE TIME THE IMAGE WAS CAPTURED, WINDS WERE COMING FROM THE SOUTHWEST AT APPROXIMATELY 6 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: ALTHOUGH THE VESSEL’S WAKE AND TRACK WERE VISIBLE IN THE IMAGE, THE SUSPECTED VESSEL ITSELF WAS NOT, AS CLOUD COVER IN THE SOUTHWEST OBSCURED THE REMAINING PORTION OF ITS PATH.

properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 803034
Incident Time: 2006-07-04 14:37:00
Nearest City: LA
Incident Type: PLATFORM
Material: METHANOL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
Skytruth Analysis
///WEB REPORT/// WHILE PRESSURING UP ON EUROPA A-6 WELL TO OPEN FBIV WE SUSPECT METHANOL UMBILICAL LEAK SUB-AREA. WE EXPERIENCED A DROP IN PRESSURE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:07 AM. STOPPED PUMPING AND ISOLATED WELLHEAD AND SHUTDOWN METHANOL PUMPS. NOTIFIED MARS LEADERSHIP AND SUB SEA SERVEILLANCE ENGINEER. WHILE TROUBLE SHOOTING THE PROBLEM AT 9:37 AM A TOTAL OF 25 LBS OF METHANOL (1050 GALLONS) WERE PUMPED AT WHICH TIME EQUIPMENT WAS SECURED AND NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE TO ENGINEERING SUPPORT TO DEVELOP A PLAN. MEETING WILL BE HELD WITH ENG. 7-5-06 @ 8:00 AM TO DETERMINE HOW MANY LBS WERE PUT IN THE GULF. IT WAS DETERMINED AT THE MEETING WE RELEASED 6930 LBS TO THE GULF.

THIS PLUGGING PLAN WAS REVIEWED AND APPROVED BY THE MMS, THE AGENCY WITH JURISDICTION OVER THIS TYPE OF OPERATION. THERE WAS NO SURFACE CONTAMINATION AS THIS RELEASE WAS AT 4600'+ ON THE SEA FLOOR.
